A1.justification: Both complete, readable 37-page PDFs describe DiverseDiT, with matching main sections and Appendices A–I. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and qualitative samples support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, one-step MeanFlow experiments, representation analyses, and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical experiments and reports revised numerical results in appendix Tables A2 and A5.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same long residual connections, three-component representation diversity loss, adaptive weighting, and training procedure. The changed ablation backbone description does not modify the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet generation at 256×256 and 512×512, including multi-step and one-step generation. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main comparisons and appendices, including the SiT, REPA, MeanFlow, DispLoss, and SRA comparisons. Bibliographic renumbering does not introduce different methods.

E3.justification: Appendix G changes the layer-selection ablation's stated backbone from SiT-XL with 28 layers to SiT-L with 24 layers. Table A7 still labels it SiT-XL and retains its numbers, so this establishes a reported setting revision, not a confirmed rerun. Other stated evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table A2 revises the training-progress analysis and supplies previously missing checkpoint FIDs. Appendix G also revises the model attributed to the layer-selection ablation. The analytical questions, remaining ablations, and CKA heatmaps are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Figure 3 retains the same statement about matching sampling seeds, noise, and class labels.

E6.justification: Appendix results are substantially revised. Table A2 changes the 50K FID from 223.93 to 89.65 and fills missing 100K, 200K, and 400K FIDs with 40.46, 31.42, and 12.69. Table A5 replaces scores across all model scales under the same stated 512×512, 400K, CFG=1.35 setting: SiT-B baseline/ours FIDs change from 43.46/33.18 to 32.77/23.96. Several reported sFID gains become ties or regressions. Main-text results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for diffusion, CKA, residual connections, diversity losses, and appendix evaluation metrics are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: explaining representation diversity, proposing DiverseDiT, accelerating convergence, and improving multi-step and one-step generation.

C2.justification: Mechanism interpretations and Appendix H's limitations and future directions are unchanged. Section F still quotes the old Table A5 values and claims consistent sFID improvement, despite the revised table containing counterexamples.

D1.justification: Appendix G revises the documented backbone and layer count for reproducing the layer-selection ablation, although Table A7 remains inconsistent. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and code/model access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography consolidates duplicate entries, including DDPM, DiT, and DINOv2, and updates bibliographic metadata. Matching the underlying works shows no added or removed research references or substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: Affiliation numbering and ordering, bibliography formatting and metadata, and the local ablation-model description are edited. The narrative, terminology, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Bibliography consolidation causes limited reflow across PDF pages 9–11. Figures, qualitative sample grids, table structures, and their placements are retained; the substantive table-value revisions are covered under E6.

improvement.justification: Table A2 improves completeness and corrects its 50K FID to agree with Figure 2; Table A5 also stops duplicating the no-CFG Table A3. However, Section F retains incompatible numbers and universal sFID-improvement claims, while Appendix G's new SiT-L identification conflicts with Table A7. These benefits and reporting inconsistencies leave the net change in overall quality uncertain.
